sections.html:
Selling fast in Voorhees depends on three things: whether the township will sign off on the house, how much the state collects at closing, and how soon a buyer can fund. Voorhees Township is a Camden County suburb of Philadelphia, with detached houses, townhouses and apartments side by side.

Most owners compare a regular listing with a cash buyer who takes the house with its flaws. Both meet the same township and state steps. The gap is how long you carry the house and how much you spend on repairs beforehand.

Voorhees covers 11.47 square miles of land in western Camden County and has 31,571 residents. Most of the housing stock went up in the decades when the population climbed from 12,919 in 1980 to 24,559 in 1990, so many houses are now old enough to need roofs, boilers and updated systems. Older names such as Kresson, Kirkwood, Glendale and Osage still show up in addresses.

Voorhees housing and income snapshot
MeasureVoorhees
Households12,503
Owner-occupied housing rate62.0%
Median value of owner-occupied homes$429,700
Median monthly owner cost with a mortgage$2,913
Median gross rent$1,754
Median household income$105,473

Only 62.0% of homes are owner-occupied, which is low for a New Jersey suburb and points to a sizable stock of condominiums, townhouses and rentals next to the detached houses. If you own a townhouse or condo, ask your association what documents it issues for a sale.

Route 73 (Berlin-Kresson Road) is the only major highway that runs through Voorhees. Interstate 295 and Route 70 reach Philadelphia by way of Cherry Hill, and Exit 32 of I-295 is partly signed for Voorhees. The Ashland station of the PATCO Speedline sits inside the township, and NJ Transit runs the 403 bus to Philadelphia.

Of the 119.81 miles of road in the township, 96.90 miles are municipal, 20.50 are county and 2.41 belong to the state, so most street repairs and plowing questions go to the township. Virtua Voorhees Hospital on Route 73 is a major local employer and a draw for buyers who want medical care close by. Mention a short drive to the train or the hospital in your listing.

The township construction office handles certificates of occupancy and continued occupancy, so call it first. Ask whether a change of owner needs a resale certificate, what the inspection covers, and how long the certificate lasts before closing.

Unpermitted work is the usual snag. A finished basement, deck or converted garage built without a permit can hold up the certificate until the permit is closed or the work removed, so pull your permit history before you sign a contract.

  • One- and two-family homes need smoke alarms with 10-year sealed batteries before a sale (N.J.A.C. 5:70-4.19).
  • That rule leaves hardwired and low-voltage alarm systems and carbon monoxide alarms alone.
  • Ask the construction office for its current checklist, inspection fee and scheduling window.

Bring the office what it asks for in one trip: your deed or tax bill to identify the lot, any permit numbers for past work, and the expected closing date. Offices move faster when the closing date is on the application, because they can tell you whether the inspection fits ahead of it.

The seller pays the state's Realty Transfer Fee, set per $500 of price by bracket. For sales over $350,000 the $200,000 to $550,000 bracket carries $4.80 per $500, and Voorhees's median of $429,700 sits inside it. Above $1 million the buyer owes an extra 1% and the seller a graduated fee.

Each name on the deed needs its own GIT/REP form. A seller who is staying in New Jersey uses GIT/REP-3 and pays nothing up front. A seller relocating out of state may owe the state a prepayment, either 2% of the price or 8.97% of the gain. Federal tax law can also exclude gain on a main home you owned and lived in for two of the last five years.

Your closing attorney sends the transfer fee affidavit in with the deed, because the county clerk may turn away a deed that arrives incomplete.

Disputes over a Voorhees assessment go to the Camden County Board of Taxation, 509 Lakeland Road in Blackwood, phone 856-225-5238. Camden County keeps the regular calendar: April 1, or May 1 after a municipal revaluation. A property valued above $1,000,000 can go straight to Tax Court.

Evidence from comparable sales carries the day at the board, not your own view of fair value. A seller who is about to close gains little from filing, but a buyer or heir who keeps the house could. Owners of a main home may qualify for the state's Homestead Benefit or Senior Freeze, and the township handles local deductions for seniors, disabled owners and people with military service.

Buyers and inspectors look first at roofs, gutters, sump pumps and heating systems, so a house with a recent roof or serviced boiler needs fewer repair credits. A cash buyer pricing the house as-is will weigh the same items.

  • Roof and gutters: ask for the install year and any warranty paperwork.
  • Basement: note any past water, and what was done about it.
  • Heating and cooling: gather service records for the last few seasons.

Which elementary school a street feeds is a question buyers raise early, so have the answer ready from the school district before you list.

A cash buyer does not need a mortgage approval or a lender's appraisal, so the sale avoids the repair demands that often come with a loan. You still owe the township sign-off, the state's closing forms and the transfer fee, and the deed still goes through your closing attorney.

The practical order is simple. Pull your permit history and close open permits. Call the construction office about the certificate and book the inspection. Ask the buyer for proof of funds and a closing date in writing. Then have your attorney review the contract, including who pays for any item the township flags. If a townhouse or condo is involved, request the association's sale documents at the same time so nothing waits on paperwork from a third party.

Compare offers by what you keep after the payoff, the transfer fee and any repairs, and by how certain the closing date is.

faqs.q: How soon could a Voorhees house sale close?
faqs.a: A cash sale often closes within a few weeks. A listed sale runs longer because of showings, the buyer's loan and any township review, so ask the construction office how long its resale inspection takes.

faqs.q: Does Voorhees need an occupancy certificate for a sale?
faqs.a: Call the township construction office, which issues the certificates of occupancy and continued occupancy used when a house changes owners. State law separately calls for 10-year sealed-battery smoke alarms in one- and two-family homes.

faqs.q: Who covers the transfer fee on a Voorhees sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays it when the deed is recorded. The buyer's extra 1% starts at $1 million, far above the $429,700 median for Voorhees homes.

faqs.q: What is the last day to contest a Voorhees assessment?
faqs.a: April 1 in Camden County, or May 1 after a revaluation. Use Form A-1 and call the Camden County Board of Taxation in Blackwood at 856-225-5238.

faqs.q: Will open permits stop a Voorhees sale?
faqs.a: They can slow the township's sign-off. Have the construction office review your permit history, then close the permits or agree in writing with the buyer on who repairs what and by when.
